title: South Korea Unveils 50-Qubit Quantum Computer, Targets 100 Qubits by 2029
key_facts: Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science (KRISS) showed a model of its 50-qubit superconducting quantum computer, still under development, at AI Festa 2026 at COEX in Seoul
The 50-qubit system and its cloud infrastructure are targeted for completion by March next year
KRISS plans 100 qubits with error correction by 2029
KRISS also develops neutral-atom computing aiming for 1,000 qubits by 2029, and diamond quantum sensors
A 20-qubit system was demonstrated in 2024 and a cloud access system unveiled in March 2025
Forum speaker Kim Hyo-sil said South Korean quantum companies roughly doubled from about 80 in 2023 to 165 in 2025; government goal is 2,000 by 2035
Article names no original outlet; BigGo Finance appears to be a rewrite
quote_evidence: KRISS plans to scale up its superconducting quantum computing to 100 qubits with error correction by 2029.
KRISS is currently pursuing both the development of a 50-qubit quantum computer system and cloud infrastructure construction, targeting completion by March next year.
why_it_matters_hint: What was shown is a model of a machine still being built; the milestones are plans.
notes: Page does not name its original outlet.
